insight.title: What the world is made of when nobody is looking
insight.subtitle: The elegant architecture of the space between us.

sections.text: Look at the palms of your hands. They feel solid, heavy, and permanent. Yet, nature hides a quiet secret about the fabric of our world. Almost everything you see is made of nothing at all. If we removed the empty space from every human, our entire species would fit inside a single sugar cube.

The atoms that build your body are like miniature, silent solar systems. Each one is a vast cathedral with a tiny center. They only feel solid because invisible fields push back against your fingers. You never truly touch a lover’s hand; you simply hover near it, held apart by a microscopic, electric push.

This hidden architecture changes how we view the mundane. We are not heavy sculptures of clay, but light, intricate clouds of energy. It is a beautiful irony that the things we find most substantial are mostly made of ghosts. In a vast emptiness, the simple act of holding on is the greatest miracle of all.

news.title: Federal government fights states' regulation of prediction markets
news.description: The federal government is suing Connecticut, Arizona and Illinois, challenging their efforts to regulate prediction market operators such as Kalshi and Polymarket.
news.why: You could have more legal options to bet on world events.

news.title: Hegseth has intervened in military promotions for more than a dozen senior officers
news.description: WASHINGTON — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has taken steps to block or delay promotions for more than a dozen Black and female senior officers across all four branches of the military, some of whom are seen as having been targeted because of their race, gender or perceived affiliation with Biden administration policies or officials, according to nine U.S. officials familiar with the process
news.why: Your family members in the military may face unexpected leadership changes.

news.title: Pete Hegseth allows troops to carry personal firearms on military bases
news.description: Defense secretary signs memo letting members request permission to carry firearms on military installations
news.why: You may now keep personal weapons with you on military installations.

news.title: Fuel crisis batters fish and chip shops, pushing up price of classic Good Friday meal
news.description: Fishing fleets are staying in port, cooking oil costs are rising and chips are no longer cheap, putting businesses across Australia under pressure

news.why: This mission brings you closer to a future of civilian spaceflight.

news.title: Moderate wine intake tied to slower biological aging in men
news.description: Researchers studying 22,495 adults in Southern Italy found that men with moderate wine intake in the traditional Mediterranean diet range showed slightly slower biomarker-based biological aging, with the lowest estimated aging signal at about 170 mL per day. The study also found that overall ethanol intake did not show the same moderate-level pattern, and higher total alcohol intake was linked to faster biological aging in dose-response analyses.
news.why: A glass of wine might help you stay younger for longer.

news.title: Iran vows 'crushing' attacks as strikes hit regional infrastructure
news.description: Iran and its allies traded fire with Israel and the United States, as Washington-linked assets across the Middle East were targeted alongside energy and civilian infrastructure -- with the month-long war on Friday showing little sign of easing.
news.why: War in this region will likely increase your monthly energy bills.
